chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir, the brother of Ishaq ibn Jarir, who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about land that a man wanted to take under qabalah, and which forms of qabalah are most permissible.

He عليه السلام said: “He may take it from its people for a specified amount and for specified years, then cultivate it and pay the kharaj. But if there are ʿuluj in it, he must not include the ʿuluj in the qabalah, for that is not halal.”

key_terms.أَرْضٍ: land that is the subject of the contract
key_terms.سِنِينَ مُسَمَّاةٍ: a fixed and defined number of years for the agreement
key_terms.عُلُوجٌ: non-Muslim laborers or foreign workers present on the land
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: it is not permissible in law
key_terms.مُسَمًّى: specified and clearly determined in amount or term
key_terms.ٱلْخَرَاجَ: the land tax due on the property
key_terms.ٱلْقَبَالَةِ: a lease or tax-farming type contractual acceptance of land

ai.seo_question: What form of qabalah for land is halal according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on taking land under qabalah through a clearly specified payment and a defined term. It also requires fulfillment of kharaj obligations and prohibits including the ʿuluj in the contract, marking limits on what may lawfully be incorporated into such an agreement.
